title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters can control event production tools
summary: Hold: the briefing treats the organiser's licensing requirement as unpublished even though its cited licensing page states that event capabilities depend on the organiser's licence. It also leaves event-type applicability open although Microsoft's comparison table documents where the production-tools setting is available.

claims.quote: Event organizers can grant production control permissions to federated (B2B) users and guest users.

claims.where: Scope: production-tools page coverage; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited Support production-tools page describes town halls.
claims.quote: Before and during a town hall, open the event meeting options to designate which specific roles or people can control the production tools.

claims.claim: People must already be added to the town hall before they can be found for the Specific people selection.
claims.quote: People must already be added to the town hall to appear in the Search for participants field.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft documents organiser assignment but no admin control over who holds production control, including per-person restrictions.
claims.quote: Who has control of production tools | No control. | Organizers can choose specific organizers, co-organizers, or presenters who can control production tools

claims.claim: The planning page lists no admin control over inviting external presenters.
claims.quote: External presenters | No control. | Can invite presenters from outside of your organization.

claims.claim: The organiser path is Calendar > town hall > View event > Manage event > Meeting options > Production tools > Who has control of production tools.
claims.quote: Select Calendar ... Select a town hall. ... Select View event > Manage event ... Select Meeting options ... In Production tools ... Who has control of production tools

claims.claim: No API or events-policy parameter is documented for assigning production control.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams production tools assignment production control events policy PowerShell Microsoft Graph virtualEventTownhall; opened Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, Graph beta virtualEventTownhall and virtualEventSettings; none documents production-control assignment.

claims.claim: Join verification is configured in Teams admin center at Meetings > Events policies > policy > Verify external presenters before joining an event.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... In the Verify external presenters before joining an event dropdown list

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires external-presenter verification.
claims.quote: To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP

claims.claim: The external-presenter verification policy defaults to No verification needed.
claims.quote: No verification needed | None | This is the default value. When organizers with this policy create events, they can decide whether external presenters must verify their identity before joining.

claims.claim: External presenters whose identities are unverified are treated as anonymous users in the event.
claims.quote: In Teams events hosted by your organization, external presenters whose identities aren't verified are treated as anonymous users in the event.

claims.claim: The existing verification policy controls whether anonymous and unverified external presenters verify their identity before joining events created by affected organisers.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control whether anonymous and unverified external presenters must verify their identity before joining events.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically documented how join verification interacts with granting production control to federated or guest users.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams production control external presenter verification applies guests federated; opened events-external-presenter-join-verification and plan-events. They document joining and production assignment separately, not that interaction.

claims.claim: Large-audience event creation is configured in Teams admin center at Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents affected organisers creating events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: Turning the scheduling setting Off after an event is scheduled prevents the user running or starting it.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: AllowTownhalls is an organiser-policy scheduling control, not a setting targeting external presenters or production-control assignment.
claims.quote: Events optimized for a large audience (On,Off) | -AllowTownhalls (Enabled,Disabled) | Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specific to an external presenter holding production control remains unpublished, so the feature-specific licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "external presenters" "production" "license"; Teams external production controls presenter license pricing 567298. Opened events-licensing and the Support production-tools page; neither states an external-controller licence requirement.

claims.claim: Teams event capabilities, including production controls, depend on the organiser's licence.
claims.quote: Event capabilities and attendee capacity vary based on the organizer's license.

claims.claim: Teams events licensing distinguishes Foundational event features and Advanced event features.
claims.quote: For Teams events, licenses fall into two categories: ... Foundational event features ... Advanced event features

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Production controls are among the Advanced event features.
claims.quote: They include the foundational capabilities plus advanced features such as event workflows, customization, production controls, monitoring, insights, and higher engagement event capacity.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: full feature-set requirement
claims.claim: Accessing the full Teams events feature set requires a licence from the Advanced event features category.
claims.quote: To access the full set of Teams events features, users must have a license from the Advanced event features category.

claims.claim: The Advanced Enterprise category lists Office 365 E1, E3, E5 and Microsoft 365 E3, E5, E7.
claims.quote: Enterprise | Not applicable | Office 365 E1, E3, E5Microsoft 365 E3, E5, E7

claims.where: Cost and licensing: organiser applicability; Open questions: licensing
claims.claim: Whether the Advanced event features licensing condition applies to the organiser is not stated.
claims.quote: Event capabilities and attendee capacity vary based on the organizer's license. ... Organizers with a license in the Advanced event features category have all foundational event capabilities plus the following advanced event features.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether that condition applies to the organiser, to the external presenter, or to both for this feature is not stated' with 'Event capabilities depend on the organiser's licence; production controls are Advanced event features. Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to the external presenter holding production control.' In Open questions, replace the licensing question with 'Which licence, if any, must the external presenter hold to receive production control?' Keep the external-presenter uncertainty, not uncertainty about the organiser. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to granting an external presenter production control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "external" "production controls" pricing metered licensing; Teams external production controls presenter license pricing 567298. Opened events-licensing and the Support production-tools page; no feature-specific price is stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for this feature at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "external" "production controls" pricing metered licensing. Opened events-licensing and production-tools documentation; search returned unrelated Azure Communication Services consumption, not a production-control meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: supplied record omissions
claims.claim: The roadmap record and supplied Message Center notice name no licence or meter for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external production controls presenter license pricing 567298; read the supplied roadmap record and MC1443517 in full. Neither names a licence requirement or usage meter.

claims.where: Scope: event-type uncertainty; Open questions: events up to 1,000 attendees
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the production-tools setting applies to events up to 1,000 attendees as well as events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: Feature | Meetings | Events up to 1,000 attendees | Events optimized for large audiences ... Who has control of production tools | [x for no.] | [x for no.] | [checkmark for yes.]
claims.fix: Replace the event-type uncertainty in Scope with 'Microsoft's feature comparison lists Who has control of production tools for events optimised for large audiences, not for the Events up to 1,000 attendees category.' Remove the corresponding Open questions bullet. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meetings-events-feature-comparison to sources. Do not equate the event category with a prohibition on smaller town halls.
